author: A Robot
objectives: Describe the apparent path of Mars across the night sky during a retrograde episode.
Explain why apparent retrograde motion occurs in the heliocentric model due to Earth overtaking slower-moving outer planets.
Contrast the geocentric and heliocentric explanations of retrograde motion.
Predict when retrograde motion will occur for a given outer planet based on orbital positions.
Compare the apparent retrograde loops of Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.

modules.description: Observe Mars's path as seen from Earth's surface during its retrograde motion.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Describe the apparent path of Mars during its retrograde episode.
Explain the visible eastward drift followed by the westward loop.
instructions: Begin by observing the stars around Mars.
Click on Mars to see its loop.

clips.changeMeaning: Mars is introduced into the scene, set to an initial position for the viewers to observe its path.
clips.narration: Welcome to our exploration of Mars and its retrograde motion.

clips.changeMeaning: Mars appears to move eastward in the night sky.
clips.narration: As we observe Mars, we see it slowly moving eastward against the backdrop of stars.

clips.changeMeaning: Mars begins to trace a loop across the sky as it enters retrograde.
clips.narration: Watch as Mars enters the westward loop during its apparent retrograde motion.

clips.changeMeaning: Mars completes its loop and prepares to move eastward again.
clips.narration: Now, Mars completes its loop and will resume its eastward motion.
